public.title: Grouped Curry
public.description: Model a curried function that accepts groups of integer arguments until it has at least arity arguments. Return null if not enough. Otherwise return the sum of the first arity arguments; ignore extras and later groups. arity is 1 through 20. This adapter tests argument collection without serializing functions. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Stop as soon as enough arguments have accumulated; ignore surplus arguments.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Append argument groups and sum only the requested prefix at completion. O(total consumed arguments) time and space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
